clusters.name: Impaired Control
items: Larger amounts or longer period than intended (DSM p.620)
Persistent desire or unsuccessful efforts to cut down (DSM p.620)
Great deal of time spent obtaining, using, or recovering (DSM p.620)
Craving or strong urge to use (DSM p.620)

clusters.name: Social Impairment
items: Recurrent use resulting in failure to fulfill major obligations (DSM p.620)
Continued use despite persistent social/interpersonal problems (DSM p.620)
Important social, occupational, or recreational activities given up (DSM p.620)

clusters.name: Risky Use
items: Recurrent use in physically hazardous situations (DSM p.620)
Continued use despite knowledge of physical/psychological problem (DSM p.620)

criteria.thresholds: >=2/11 criteria within a 12-month period; Tolerance/Withdrawal excluded under legitimate medical supervision (DSM p.620-621)

epidemiology.prevalence: 12-month prevalence 0.3% in adolescents (12-17) and adults; 2.4% nonmedical use (DSM p.623, p.628)
epidemiology.sex_ratio: Equal in US, higher female prevalence internationally (DSM p.624)
epidemiology.onset_age_typical: Peak prevalence in young adults aged 18-29 (0.5%) (DSM p.623)
epidemiology.heritability: Significant genetic contribution confirmed in twin studies (DSM p.624)
epidemiology.prognosis: Escalation from social misuse to daily dependence in youth, or prescription escalation with doctor shopping in adults (DSM p.623-624)

etiology.genetic: Twin studies show genetic risk increasing from adolescence to adulthood (DSM p.624)
etiology.neurobiology: GABA-A PAMs increase Cl- opening frequency; Barbiturates increase duration & direct opening; VTA disinhibition increases Nucleus Accumbens dopamine (StahlNeuro p.257-262, p.553-556)
etiology.environmental: High prescription availability, family/peer diversion, peer pressure, and self-medication of anxiety/insomnia (DSM p.624; Dulcan p.223; StahlKids p.6)

first_line: Gradual Taper with long-acting BZD (Diazepam or Clonazepam) (Dulcan p.223; StahlNeuro p.561)
CBT for underlying anxiety and insomnia (Dulcan p.482)
second_line: Clonidine for autonomic hyperarousal in withdrawal (StahlKids p.143-144)
Flumazenil for acute single-dose BZD intoxication reversal ONLY (StahlNeuro p.262)
key_side_effects: Life-threatening withdrawal seizures (20-30%) and DTs on abrupt cessation (DSM p.629-630)
Flumazenil-induced fatal seizures in chronic users (StahlNeuro p.262)
treatment.monitoring: Monitor BP and HR during Clonidine titration; urine drug screens; strict parental medication control in youth (StahlKids p.6, p.144)

items: Urine drug screens detect long-acting BZDs up to 7 days (DSM p.625)
K-SADS-PL structured interview for pediatric SUD (Dulcan p.70)
key_numbers: 7 days - urine detection window for long-acting BZDs like Diazepam (DSM p.625)
>=2 - CRAFFT score indicating high SUD risk (Dulcan p.230)
>=1 - Level 1 Substance Use score requiring Level 2 assessment (DSM p.844)

items: Alcohol Intoxication/Withdrawal - identical presentation, distinguished by breath odor and blood alcohol level (DSM p.564, p.627)
Subdural Hematoma / Head Trauma from falls - requires brain CT/MRI (DSM p.625; Dulcan p.121)
Hypoglycemia - mimics intoxication and withdrawal, requires glucometer test (DSM p.566; Dulcan p.608)
Independent Psychiatric Disorder - anxiety/depression persisting >1 month post-withdrawal (DSM p.204, p.632)
key_numbers: 1 month - persistence duration post-withdrawal required to diagnose independent disorder (DSM p.204, p.632)
0 BAL - blood alcohol level in pure sedative intoxication (DSM p.627)

high_yield: Sedative/BZD withdrawal CAN be life-threatening with Grand Mal seizures (20-30%) and delirium; ALWAYS taper gradually (DSM p.629-630; Dulcan p.223)
Tolerance and withdrawal DO NOT count toward Use Disorder diagnosis if medication is taken under legitimate medical supervision (DSM p.621)
BZDs are PAMs increasing GABA-A Cl- channel opening FREQUENCY; Barbiturates increase DURATION and act as direct agonists at high doses (StahlNeuro p.260, p.556)
Alpha-1 GABA-A subunit mediates sedation/amnesia (Z-drugs target); Alpha-2/3 mediate anxiolysis (StahlNeuro p.260, p.422)
Flumazenil triggers fatal seizures in chronic BZD users or mixed TCA overdose (StahlNeuro p.262)
Avoid BZDs as first-line in youth due to lack of efficacy, addiction risk, and paradoxical disinhibition (Dulcan p.213, p.482)
